newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan ruling party wants polls by year end - report.
newsitem.headline: Japan ruling party wants polls by year end - report.

text.p: Japan's Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) has urged Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto to dissolve parliament in October and hold general elections within this year, a daily newspaper reported on Thursday.

Top officials of the LDP, the largest party in Japan's three-party ruling coalition, called on Hashimoto, the party president, to exercise his exclusive power to call snap elections as early as possible before an unpopular tax increase takes effect next April, the daily Mainichi Shimbun reported.

The officials cited the need to preempt an opposition campaign against the April consumption tax rise -- to five percent from three percent -- and to act before a minor revolt in the coalition's junior party can gather momentum, it said.

Hashimoto, who must call elections for the 500-seat Lower House of parliament by next July, said at the weekend he would decide on the autumn parliamentary schedule after assessing gross domestic product (GDP) figures for the April-June quarter, to be released later this month.
The prime minister also cited the need to monitor Sunday's referendum in the southern prefecture of Okinawa on trimming the heavy concentration of U.S. military bases there.
The U.S. bases became the subject of an explosive political dispute between the central government and Okinawa last year after the rape of an Okinawa schoolgirl by three U.S. servicemen.

Hashimoto took office in January at the helm of a coalition of the LDP, the Social Democratic Party and New Party Sakigake, which united in June 1994 to oust the reformist coalition that prevailed in the last general elections in July 1993.

Sakigake was shaken last week by a revolt which saw a handful of members leave to form a new party to contest elections. The new group has not made clear whether it will work with the government or join the opposition.
